input: Where can I find info about support orgs and shelters for UM, incl. local options?
expected_output: You can find information about support organizations and shelters for undocumented migrants (UM), including local options, on the Stichting LOS website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and for shelters: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Additionally, the Red Cross Helpful Information website provides details about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/.
context:
['Q: What are relevant websites with information about / for UM? A: 
* On the website of **LOS** you can find information about support organizations: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/organisaties and shelters in the Netherlands: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. 
* On the website **Helpful Information** from the Red Cross you can find information about local organizations in different cities: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/', 'Q: Why is somebody that is undocumented often in a vulnerable position? A: Undocumented migrants are regarded as a vulnerable group within society. They do not have a residence permit and, because of their limited rights, they quickly find themselves in unsafe or unhealthy situations. Because of their vulnerable position, they are easy prey for exploitation at the hands of bad employers, slum landlords or human traffickers.

Also, they are not entitled to social benefits and cannot take out health insurance (the 1998 Dutch Benefit Entitlement (Residence Status) Act; Koppelingswet). They have only a very limited right to assistance and facilities from the government and other agencies. As a result, they can easily get into trouble. The Red Cross provides help to everyone, including undocumented migrants.', 'Q: When is somebody undocumented? A: An undocumented migrant is a person who has no right of residence in a country. They have no documents confirming a right of residence, such as a visa. Their work, residence or study visa has expired, or they may never have had one. 

They are mainly migrants who:
- have had their residence application rejected, for example asylum seekers whose application for asylum has been rejected;
- have not applied for a residence permit, either for regular residence or asylum;
- are victims of human trafficking;
- do not have a work permit, for example domestic workers.

EU citizens do not need to apply for a residence permit to be in the Netherlands legally. Migrants from the EU can therefore never be undocumented."
', "Q: What is a Dublin claim? A: When somebody asks asylum in the Netherlands, their finger prints will be checked in an EU database. If their fingerprint is registered in another EU country, that country is responsible for proceeding the asylum procedure. In that case somebody gets a Dublin claim and has to return to the EU country where the fingerprint was taken. They cannot get asylum in the Netherlands. This is because according to the EU’s Dublin Regulation, somebody's asylum procedure must be carried out in the first country of arrival. 

The Dublin claim ends after 18 months. So if somebody is capable of staying under the radar for 18 months, then he/ she can request asylum in the Netherlands.

It is very hard for people with a Dublin Claim to get support. For example often local shelter programs do not provide shelter to people with a Dublin claim.", 'Q: Where can I find information about the programs of the Red Cross for Undocumented Migrants? A: As Red Cross we provide workshops to UM about health care, working rights, healthy habits, clear communication and first aid. We also have a [website](https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl) with information about local aid organizations and we help people through our WhatsApp Helpline. Besides that people that are UM can also be in our food program or shelter program. This is always through the connection with a partner organization. For more information on our programs, you can have a look at our website: https://www.rodekruis.nl/wat-doen-wij/hulp-in-nederland/ondersteuning-ongedocumenteerde-migranten/', 'Q: Where can I find information about the shelter rights for Undocumented Migrants? A: You can find information about different shelter rights on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/opvang-en-onderdak

In general people have the right to rent a house, but not from social corperate housing. There is no general right for shelter for people who are undocumented and most homeless shelters refuse people without residence permit. This means that housing is a very big challenge for people that are undocumented.

In some cities there are BBB (Bed, Bad, Brood) shelters for undocumeted migrants or municipality shelter programs for undocumented migrants. They often work with criteria, for example that they have a rejected asylum request and that there is a perspective on a new asylum request. You can find information on this on helpful information https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/ or on the website of LOS: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang', 'Q: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? A: What is our role on the helpdesk with regard to shelter questions from UM? 
The Red Cross doesn’t have shelters ourselves. Therefore we cannot always help somebody. The Red Cross 
does have a shelter program, but this is only for 10 days and when there is a partner organization involved. 
Our goal on the helpdesk is to get a good understanding of the situation in order to: 
• make a right referral, to a local support organization or to the district so they can help somebody further with support and advice. 
• is known with day shelters (if he doesn’t know them yet).', 'Q: What does LVV stand for? A: LVV stands for Landelijke Vreemdelingen Voorziening. The LVV program was a government / municipality program where people who were rejected for asylum could get a place in a 24-hour shelter for a maximum of 18 months. If they were admitted to the program, they would have access to 24hour shelter, an allowance, professional guidance and different activities.

Social workers supported them to find a solution to their situation: a residence permit, migrating to another country or returning to their home country.

The Dutch government decided to end the finance for the LVV from 2025 onwards. For 2025 the cities Amsterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Groningen have decided to continue the shelter program for Undocumented Migrants without the finance of the national government. Only Rotterdam decided to stop. Information on how to access the local municipality programs can be found on HIA.', "Q: What does BBB stand for A: BBB stands for Bed, Bad, Brood. The local shelter locations for undocumented migrants are often called like this. Throughout the country there are several BBB's. You can find them on this website: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang 

Often they are full or they work with stricked criteria, such as a legal perspective on a new asylum request. So never just send somebody to these locations, but check with the local organization or with the TC.", "Q: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program? 
 A: How can people enter a BBB / municipality shelter program?
Not everybody can access the municipality shelter programs or BBB's. There are certain criteria. For example people need to have asked asylum in the past. And people with a Dublin claim can often not enter the local shelter programs. In order to get access to the shelter, people should go to one of the screening locations or get into contact with the BBB's. They they can get more information, share their story and perhaps be admitted in the program.

Information on the local possibilities can be found on Helpful Information and on https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang. Never send somebody directly to a BBB, but always check first with TC."]

input: If UM lost access to all support orgs, what new risks might they face in NL?
expected_output: If undocumented migrants (UM) lose access to all support organizations in the Netherlands, they face increased risks of exploitation by bad employers, slum landlords, or human traffickers due to their vulnerable position and lack of rights. Without support, they have even less access to shelter, healthcare, and basic needs, making them more likely to end up in unsafe or unhealthy situations. They are also not entitled to social benefits or health insurance, so losing support further limits their ability to get help, increasing the likelihood of homelessness, health problems, and social isolation.

input: How do limited rights, lack of benefits, and housing restrictions increase UM vulnerability to exploitation?
expected_output: Limited rights, lack of benefits, and housing restrictions make undocumented migrants (UM) highly vulnerable to exploitation. Without a residence permit, they have very limited rights and cannot access social benefits or health insurance. Most homeless shelters refuse people without a residence permit, and they cannot rent from social housing corporations. This forces UM into unsafe or unhealthy situations, making them easy targets for exploitation by bad employers, slum landlords, or human traffickers. Their lack of legal protection and support increases their risk of being taken advantage of.

input: Analyze how limited rights to social benefits and health insurance increase UM vulnerability to exploitation.
expected_output: Limited rights to social benefits and health insurance make undocumented migrants (UM) more vulnerable to exploitation because they cannot access basic support or protection from the government. Without social benefits, they have no financial safety net, making them dependent on informal or unsafe work, where they are at risk of being exploited by bad employers or landlords. The inability to take out health insurance means they may avoid seeking medical help, leading to unsafe or unhealthy situations. This lack of rights and support makes it easier for others to take advantage of their vulnerable position.

input: Identify the criteria distinguishing stateless persons from undocumented migrants in Dutch immigration law.

input: Examine the challenges faced by stateless individuals lacking any legal residency or nationality documentation.
expected_output: Stateless individuals without legal residency or nationality documentation face significant challenges. They have no recognized legal status, which means they cannot access basic rights such as social benefits, health insurance, or legal employment. This makes them highly vulnerable to exploitation by employers, landlords, or traffickers. They are often excluded from most government assistance and shelter programs, and finding housing is extremely difficult since most shelters require a residence permit. Their lack of documentation leaves them in unsafe or unhealthy situations and makes it easy for them to get into trouble or be taken advantage of.

- Amsterdam", 'Q: How do winter shelters function? A: There are two different types of winter shelter. You have the permanent winter shelter and the Cold Weather Regulation. The municipality can decide if they want to organize a permanent winter shelter and if this is accessible for undocumented migrants or not. They have the legal duty to organize the Cold Weather Regulation when temperatures go below 0 degrees as it becomes too dangerous to sleep outside. The Cold Weather Regulation can be opened in the period from the 1st of November until the 1st of April.
Undocumented migrants always have access access to the Cold Weather Regulation, but not always to the permanent winter shelters. 

Large cities (Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague and Utrecht) coordinate the Cold Weather Regulation together. So they often open and close at the same time. 

On the *Heplful Information website (HIA)*[https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/] you can find the opening times of the Cold Weather Regulation and winter shelters per city. ', 'Q: Where can I find information about shelters for UM? A: On Helpful Information you can find information about local shelters for UM: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/
Also on the website of LOS you can find information: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/noodopvang
', 'Q: Where can I find information about the medical rights of UM? 
 A: You can find information on the website of Stichting Los: https://www.stichtinglos.nl/content/gezondheidszorg', 'Q: Do people have the right to see a family doctor? A: Yes, people always have the right to see a family doctor. The doctor can reimburse the costs with the CAK. 
You can refer people to this website for information on how family doctors work in the Netherlands: 
* https://gpinfo.nl/1-dutch-healthcare', 'Q: Reimbursement of medical costs. A: * Important: it is differently arranged per target group (e.g. asylum seekers, undocumented, EU migrants. You can find more information on the website of CAK: https://www.hetcak.nl/zakelijk/via-welke-regeling-declareren/ 
• People who are undocumented have the right to receive all the necessary medical aid (medisch noodzakelijke zorg). This is care that is also in the basic health insurance. The costs are reimbursed by the CAK. you can always send the following letter to someone, they can show this letter to their doctor: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf 
• Here you can see what is in the basic package: https://www.zorginstituutnederland.nl/Verzekerde+zorg/basispakket-zorgverzekeringswet-zvw

What services can be reimbursed:
* General practitioners and dentists (for oral care up to the age of 18) are reimbursed for 80% by the CAK if the undocumented patient cannot pay this themselves. The CAK expects the healthcare provider to first try to recover the costs from the patient without a residence permit. Asking for payment can deter migrants without a residence permit and therefore hinders treatment compliance.
* You can only refer an undocumented patient to pharmacies, hospitals, Wlz and mental health care institutions with which the CAK has a contract. The list of contracted institutions changes regularly, for a current list visit Hetcak.nl/zakelijk/verzekeringen/onverzekerbare-vreemdelingen. 
* Since 2014, there has been a personal contribution of 5 euros per medicine, unless delivery via a blister/baxter is prescribed.
* Emergency care, by both contracted and non-contracted hospitals, is reimbursed for 80%.
* Obstetric care is 100% reimbursed.

input: What steps can undocumented migrants in NL take to access GP or emergency medical care?
expected_output:
Undocumented migrants in the Netherlands have the right to see a doctor, including a GP (huisarts) and emergency care. Steps they can take:

1. **Contact a GP (huisarts):** They can visit a family doctor. If they have a fixed address, it is best to register with a GP for ongoing care. If they have trouble finding a GP, they can ask for help from organizations like the Red Cross or specialized organizations for undocumented migrants.

2. **Use specialized organizations:** In cities with specialized organizations, these can help undocumented migrants access medical care and may have networks of doctors willing to help.

3. **Emergency care:** For urgent medical needs, they can go to the emergency post at a hospital. Hospitals have a legal duty to help in emergencies, regardless of insurance or residence status.

4. **After-hours care:** For urgent issues outside office hours, they should call the huisartsenpost (out-of-hours GP service). If they cannot do this themselves, the Red Cross may assist.

5. **Bring supporting documents:** If a doctor is hesitant, migrants can show the Red Cross letter explaining their rights and the CAK reimbursement for costs: https://helpfulinformation.redcross.nl/files/Brief-zorgverlening-ongedocumenteerde-migranten-landelijk.pdf

6. **Cost reimbursement:** Medical costs for undocumented migrants are often reimbursed by the CAK, especially for necessary care.

For more information or help, they can contact the Red Cross Amsterdam-Amstelland at heretohelp.amsterdam@rodekruis.nl.

input: Can undocumented migrants report labor exploitation to Dutch police without risk of immediate deportation?

It is important to recognize their rights and refer them to specialized organizations for help.
